questions.question: A team adopts a second AI host for the same internal MCP server. Which statement is true about the server's code?
options: It must be rebuilt once for every extra host that joins
It is re-registered by the registry for each new host
It needs a new branch of logic for each host it serves
It answers every host's client with the same result each time
questions.explanation: A server's capability contract is fixed by the specification and does not vary by host, so adding a host is a client-side cost, never a server change.

questions.question: On a remote Streamable HTTP deployment with no gateway in front of it, which role implements OAuth 2.0 Protected Resource Metadata?
options: The server author, since the MUST is written for the server
The end user, since consent metadata names what they saw
The platform or gateway operator, since it runs the process
The registry publisher, since metadata sits with a listing
questions.explanation: The specification makes Protected Resource Metadata a server MUST, so without a gateway in front of it, the server author's own implementation is the one that has to carry it.

questions.question: A gateway now fronts that same server. Which role becomes responsible for validating the Origin header before a request reaches the server's own code?
options: The security and governance owner, who writes the policy
The gateway operator, who terminates the connection first
The server author, who still owns every transport check here
The host and client developer, who builds the OAuth client
questions.explanation: Once a gateway terminates the connection, it is the first code to see the Origin header, so the platform or gateway operator inherits the MUST that the server author carried alone under plain HTTP.

questions.question: A stdio deployment needs a credential for an internal API call. Per the specification's transport guidance, where should that credential come from?
options: An OAuth access token negotiated over the stdio channel itself
A bearer token embedded directly in the tool's input schema
The environment the operator configures before the process starts
A session id the server assigns on the connection's first call
questions.explanation: STDIO implementations SHOULD NOT follow the OAuth authorization flow and instead retrieve credentials from the environment, which is the platform or gateway operator's responsibility to configure.

questions.question: A curated requirement catalog includes a MUST whose default role is deliberately left unset because no single one of the six roles cleanly owns it. What should a responsibility matrix built from that catalog do with it?
options: Drop it from the matrix, since a MUST NOT is not a MUST
Assign it to the publisher by default, since it lists last
Assign it to the end user by default, since they consent
Report it as a gap so the team assigns an explicit owner
questions.explanation: A responsibility matrix should surface an unowned MUST as a gap rather than guess an owner, because a silently misassigned requirement is as risky as an unassigned one.

questions.question: A host and client developer needs an SDK that ships new protocol features before a spec release and resolves critical bugs within a week. Which SDK tier commits to that bar?
options: Tier 1, since it commits to full conformance and fast fixes
Any tier, since tiers only describe documentation quality, not speed
Tier 2, since six months is close enough for production use
Tier 3, since experimental SDKs move the fastest of the three
questions.explanation: Tier 1 is the only tier that commits to shipping new features before or alongside a spec release and fixing critical bugs within seven days, the bar this scenario requires.
